name: FSAE 2027 -- PUCPR Racing -- rocker concept H2
author: Vinicius Trento
notes: Rocker/rod concept H2: Concept H2 (550 lb/in): concept H's front redrawn so the MR does not fall in bump (a larger rocker); rear of concept H (the team's). Built by scripts/rocker_concepts.py from projects/rocker_concepts/concept_H2.json (MR 0.506 is a comparison query, not a choice; packaging checked to ±36 mm of wheel travel, which needs a bump stop and a droop limiter). See projects/rocker_concepts/concept_front_550.md.

hardpoints.origin: chassis pick-ups from CAD 'Xasis 33.3' (PSD, PST), placement forward -Y, left -X, up -Z; ISO origin at CAD (0, -120.4, 75) mm; other points from the project

targets.name: Front roll centre height
targets.rationale: Low RC keeps most lateral transfer elastic (tunable) and jacking small; 25-45 mm band.

targets.name: Rear roll centre height
targets.rationale: Rear above front tilts the roll axis nose-down: directional stability, more geometric transfer at the rear.

targets.name: Front FVSA length
targets.rationale: Camber gain ~57.3/FVSA deg/mm recovers 60-80 % of roll over the first 25 mm of travel without a nervous RC.

targets.name: Roll gradient
targets.rationale: 0.8-1.5 deg/g: enough roll to use the camber gain, little enough to keep camber negative on the outer tyre.
targets.reference: Milliken RCVD Ch.16; FSAE design reports

targets.name: Static camber
targets.rationale: Offsets the +roll camber the outer tyre sees at 1.5 g.

targets.name: Front anti-dive
targets.rationale: Mid-band of the 5-10 % the team asked for; limits pitch under braking without killing brake feel.

targets.name: Ackermann at 10 deg outer
targets.rationale: Tight FSAE hairpins favour near-true Ackermann at low speed.

targets.name: Chassis torsion / roll stiffness
targets.rationale: 3-5x keeps the front/rear roll-stiffness split meaningful.

design_log.title: Chassis CAD pick-ups adopted as the master
design_log.decision: Inboard UCA/LCA pick-ups (16) taken from the chassis CAD 'Xasis 33.3' (PSD/PST frame nodes) via scripts/import_chassis_pickups.py; project switched to hardpoint mode.
design_log.rationale: The chassis team moved the pick-ups within the rules suspension gave them; front-view geometry is nearly unchanged (camber gain change < 1e-4 deg/mm, RC height -1.8 / -1.2 mm). Consequences recorded: front RC migration -0.200 -> -0.278 mm/mm, bump steer ~0.002 deg/mm both axles (tie rods sized for the old arms), rear anti-squat 0 -> 15 %, front UCA/LCA ratio 0.82 -> 0.77, rear wishbone sweep e/a above 2.
design_log.alternatives: Keep the synthesis pick-ups and ask the chassis to move its nodes 30-58 mm.
design_log.author: Vinicius Trento

design_log.title: Starting layout for pushrods, rockers and dampers (to be refined)
design_log.decision: Front: pushrod on the LCA 40 mm inboard of the LBJ to a rocker on the top tube (bulkhead to front hoop), damper along that tube. Rear: pushrod on the LCA to a rocker just behind the rear frame, routed behind the UCA rear leg (33 mm clearance); damper forward over the rear frame. Both arms placed tangential at ride and sized for MR 0.80 with equal damper margins (stroke 57 mm is an ESTIMATE).
design_log.rationale: Seed to evaluate, not a choice: MR 0.80 with the 220 lb/in springs gives ~3.2 / 2.9 Hz (F/R, wheel-rate frequency); the springs alone give ~1.2 deg/g, so an anti-roll bar is needed for 1.0 deg/g. Rocker brackets, damper bodies and the engine/diff package are not checked: the chassis team places them in CAD.
design_log.alternatives: Rear pushrod in front of the UCA front leg (4.5 mm clearance: rejected); rear pullrod to a low rocker (MR 0.80 not reachable with these arms); MR from ~0.5 (550 lb/in springs) to ~1.0.
design_log.author: Vinicius Trento

design_log.title: Rocker layout: concept A, refined
design_log.decision: Pushrods to bell-crank rockers on the upper side structure, coil-overs lying fore-aft along the frame sides (concept A of projects/rocker_concepts/README.md), refined against the chassis update of 2026-10-15 and the engine placed on its mounts: front rod on an upright clevis on the kingpin axis 53.5 mm above the LBJ; rear rocker moved 95 mm forward onto the Tri_Tras upper rail. Inputs in projects/rocker_concepts/concept_A_refined.json; report in projects/rocker_concepts/concept_A_refined.md.
design_log.rationale: Chosen by the designer from the three concepts compared on 2026-10-14. The refined layout misses no evaluator threshold on either axle (both corners, to the damper end stops, full rack travel); front LCA bending from the rod removed; rear chain-line gap 8.2 -> 33.5 mm (estimate). MR 0.80 at ride and the 220 lb/in springs remain open decisions (design_intent query arguments).
design_log.alternatives: Concept B (pushrod, transverse coil-overs over the top: needs a new rear member, rocker on the main-hoop brace) and concept C (low pullrod: regressive MR, rod loads 2.4x wheel load, no anti-roll-bar location found). Front fallback recorded in the refinement: rod on the LCA rear leg 39.5 mm from the ball joint with its own rocker (no fails, LCA bending -54 %).
design_log.author: Vinicius Trento

design_log.title: Rocker layout: concept DF (rockers and coil-overs at frame nodes)
design_log.decision: Front of concept D: pushrod from the LCA rear leg 45 mm from the ball joint to a rocker 49.0 mm from the front-hoop side node; coil-over almost vertical behind the hoop's lower leg to an eye 57.5 mm from the front-hoop bottom node. Rear of concept F (refined): pullrod from a clevis on the UCA (rod end 25.5 mm off the front leg, 62 mm from the upper ball joint) to a rocker 53.7 mm from the rear lower node, outboard of the chain; coil-over up to an eye 56.4 mm from the rear upper node. Inputs in projects/rocker_concepts/concept_DF.json; comparison in projects/rocker_concepts/concept_nodes_DEF.md.
design_log.rationale: Chosen by the designer to mount the rocker pivots and coil-over chassis ends at welded frame nodes instead of mid-span (concept A refined: 94 / 199 mm front, 95 / 188 mm rear from the nearest node). Zero evaluator fails on both axles, node checks and the inner tie-rod joint / boot envelope included. MR 0.80 at ride and the 220 lb/in springs remain open decisions (design_intent query arguments).
design_log.alternatives: Concept D rear (rod at mid-span of the LCA front leg, about 270 MPa bending at ride on 25.4x1.2; coil-overs in the differential's space); concept E (high rockers, front coil-over boxed in by near-zero gaps); concept F front (refined: pivot 61.2 mm from its node and two gaps at the 5 mm limit, because both low front nodes are LCA pivots and the coil-over crosses the rack line).
design_log.author: Vinicius Trento

design_log.title: Rear rocker layout: concept H, 550 lb/in springs at MR 0.506
design_log.decision: Rear of concept H: pushrod (in compression) from a clevis on the UCA rear leg (24.9 mm off its centreline, 50 mm from the upper ball joint) up to a rocker 53.5 mm from the UCA rear pivot node (-1461, 210, 328); coil-over down to an eye 52.1 mm from the LCA rear pivot node (-1441, 175, 129). Rear springs 550 lb/in; MR 0.506 at ride keeps the wheel rate of 220 lb/in at 0.80 (24.7 N/mm). Packaging was checked to +-36 mm of wheel travel, which needs a rear bump stop and droop limiter (design_intent; about 10 mm of damper stroke left at each end). The front stays on concept DF (220 lb/in, MR 0.80, same 24.7 N/mm) until a front for 550 lb/in is chosen. Inputs in projects/rocker_concepts/concept_H.json; comparison in projects/rocker_concepts/concept_550_lbin.md.
design_log.rationale: Chosen by the designer from the three 550 lb/in concepts G, H, I. DF's rear pullrod ran through its own coil-over (gap -37.2 mm, seen in SolidWorks); H's rear passes every evaluator check, has no part-to-part interference in the solids, a rising MR (0.496 / 0.506 / 0.512) and was first or second under all five comparison lenses (packaging, structure, kinematics, integration, unmodelled risks). MR 0.506 and the +-36 mm travel limit are design_intent query arguments.
design_log.alternatives: G rear (pushrod from the LCA: lowest loads and lateral load into the UCA rear node, about 1.0 kN, but its rocker hub overlaps the frame and the engine tab and it is the least robust to 5 mm moves); I rear (best measured clearances but both coil-overs 72-102 mm from the centreline, in the unmodelled differential's space). Open items for H rear: about 2.1 kN per side pushed inboard into the UCA rear node at ride (no cross tube there), rocker hub needs a bracket detail, chain 11.4 mm and eyes 6.9 mm (estimates), differential envelope not modelled.
